messages.subject_clean: R held back by autopkgtest fail in Rdpack, also fails some CRAN tests
messages.body_plain:
The R package(s) (source is r-base, key package is r-base-core and package
r-base wraps some more useful auxliairy packages around) is once again held
back from migrating from unstable (where I uploaded it 15 days ago when it
was released) to testing because some of the 1000+ reverse dependencies
fail. [1] A few days ago it was several packages including IIRC some from
BioConductor, now it is down to just one: r-cran-rdpack. It is current to
upstream (2.6.2) and I note that it also fails some (but not all) tests at
CRAN [2].

Might I ask both the upstream maintainer for Rdpack (George, CC'ed) as well
as the Debian package maintainer team reached here via the list to take a
look and possibly unplug Rdpack (aka r-cran-rdpack) so that R 4.4.3 gets into
Debian testing?

Many thanks,  Dirk

[1] https://qa.debian.org/excuses.php?package=r-base
[2] https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_Rdpack.html

-- 
dirk.eddelbuettel.com | @eddelbuettel | edd at debian.org

messages.body_plain:
Hi Andreas,

I just checked both of these packages (r-cran-erm and
r-cran-raschsampler) to upgrade them if needed, but they are
up-to-date with upstream.

Best wishes,

   Julian

On Mon, Mar 18, 2024 at 08:18:26AM +0100, Andreas Tille wrote:
> Hi Julian,
> 
> Am Sun, Mar 17, 2024 at 01:17:44PM +0000 schrieb Julian Gilbey:
> > On Mon, Mar 11, 2024 at 03:47:42PM +0100, Andreas Tille wrote:
> > > Hi R-pkg team members,
> > > [...]
> > 
> > > Julian Gilbey <jdg at debian.org>:
> > >  r-cran-erm
> > >  r-cran-raschsampler
> > 
> > I realise I have not used these in a while;
> 
> As a general remark:  I personally use only about 1% of those r-*
> packages I've put my name as Uploader - possibly less.  What matters for
> me personally is that we provide a working scientific environment to our
> users which includes all those R packages which are mostly born out of
> dependencies from other packages or explicit user requests.
> 
> > if someone else would be
> > able to take these over, please feel free to do so!
> 
> In the past this usually endet up by putting my ID to Uploaders.
> Changelog from r-cran-erm has one upload done by Dylan (in CC).  This
> would not really help in the current situation since my intention of the
> initial mail was fo find someone who might take over those mass-uploads
> I did in the past.  Just adding my ID and than do nothing does not make
> sense.
> 
> Alternatively we might start with some removals.  Neither r-cran-erm nor
> r-cran-raschsampler have any rdepends except for science-statistics
> metapackage from where these can easily be removed.  Popcon votes for
> both [1],[2] are not extraordinarily high bit we have some remaining use
> cases.
> 
> The question is: Do we want to remove the package or does someone think
> that firing up `routine-update` on these packages once in a while and
> `dput` the result is a feasible task?  Its a semi-automated process not
> draining much time but someone just has to do it.  Otherwise removal
> seems to be the better option to me.
> 
> Kind regards
>      Andreas.
>

messages.body_plain:
Following up on this thread, with the new Rdpack now in (thanks, Michael) the
R package 'r-base' is now held back by SparseArray aka r-bioc-sparsearray:

  https://qa.debian.org/excuses.php?package=r-base

where we see
 - on amd64 2 fails, 26998 (!!) passes
 - on arm64 2 fails, 26998 (!!) passes
 - on ppc64el 2 fails, 26998 (!!) passes

The fails look like they could be unrelated / due to a change in testthat or
alike.  It would be nice if one of you group maintainers could maybe get in
contact with upstream (I have not checked at BioConductor) but also 'park'
these two tests (at least temporarily) so that R can proceed to testing.

Thanks,  Dirk
 
--

messages.body_plain:
Le Fri, Mar 21, 2025 at 08:37:54PM -0500, Dirk Eddelbuettel a écrit :
> R package 'r-base' is now held back by SparseArray aka r-bioc-sparsearray:

Hello Dirk and everybody,

sorry for my late action: a bad triangle of misconfigured self-hosted
email server, postponed remote work, and forgotten AC adapter left me in
the « I'll fix it tomorrow » mode for longer than expected.

On the Bioconductor side SparseArray happily passes the same tests with
R 4.4.3, so I do not understand where the problem is.  In the end I just
uploaded an update of r-bioc-sparsearray where I have removed the
Testsuite field from debian/control to let r-base migrate.

By the way, the next Bioconductor release is scheduled for April 16th,
as usual a bit after the R release.  While this does not play well with
Debian's soft freeze on April 15th, it means that Bioconductor is moving
on.  If there is no further evidence of real breakage (such as
r-bioc-sparsearray downstream package tests failing), I suggest we just
keep the tests turned off until the next Bioconductor transition.

Have a nice day,

Charles
